name: Material variants
summary: Swap the constitutive model (elastic, weakly-compressible fluid, snow plasticity) and study how each behaves and optimizes under the same control task. The most visually striking axis for the demo.

tasks.title: Shape-matching across materials (where the constitutive differences bite)
tasks.note: fluid-vs-snow found the constitutive model barely moves COM ballistics on the throw task — the differences were an optimization-landscape effect on a near-ballistic loss. The honest next step (flagged in that task's limitations and training page): swap the COM-to-target loss for a task that forces large internal deformation — match a target outline / pack into a mold / sustained contact — where recoverable elastic energy and the active snow plastic clamp shape the optimized quantity directly. Tests whether the smooth->kinked ordering of optimization difficulty (fluid<elastic<snow) sharpens, and whether a softened plastic clamp recovers a usable gradient for snow. Also map each material's stability lr ceiling instead of hand-picked lr.

tasks.title: Implement Nondifferentiable Material Variants
tasks.note: Let’s start simple. Implement a nondifferentiable forward simulatiodemonstrating the difference between solids, liquids, and snow. Show these materials under a few different settings. Verify they are behaving as expected. This is primarily a learning task, meant to get a grounding with these new materials, and demonstrate what they look like. Make sure to update the training report, so that I actually learn from this task.

tasks.title: Fluids, snow, and solids as differentiable simulations
tasks.note: These look really cool. Now let’s build a simple differentiable implementation of each and see what it takes to get meaningful gradients. When you tried this before the gradients were bad and the particles exhibited erroneous behavior. Be sure to test iteratively to check that it’s functional, examining images as needed. If we can’t get meaningful gradients just report so honestly and explain or theorize why. Make sure to give some nice visuals and update training materials.

tasks.title: Varying Liquid Viscosity
tasks.note: Implement a simulation of a fluid under varying viscosities and demonstrate the differences in their behavior in a few settings. The viscosity should vary dramatically, like from honey to oil.
